the elucidation of the mechanisms of AID and AID-like enzymes.
the development of novel yeast selectable systems to analyze the functional properties of AID in vivo and to search for cofactors of AID induced sommatic hypermutations.
the development of new methods for the analysis of the molecular basis of the AID induced somatically acquired diversity of the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytidine deaminate AID is a multifunctional enzyme, which is able to deaminate DNA as well as RNA, while its homologue APOBEC1 is an mRNA editing enzyme.
APOBEC1 and AID have distinct functional properties.
AID is a cytidine deamidase, whereas APOBEC1 is a cytidinase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AID is a deaminating enzyme, but not a deaminating editing enzyme.
AID and AID like proteins are not only able to deaminate single stranded DNA in the nucleus, but also RNA and double stranded DNA in the cytoplasm.

yeast can be used to study the functional properties of cytidine de-aminases and to identify cofactors for AID activity in vivo.
